task.title: Remove the retry cap from the payment client
task.description: Retries keep exhausting before the upstream recovers. Remove the retry cap so payment requests retry until they succeed.

proposal.summary: Remove the finite retry cap from the payment client so payment requests keep retrying until they succeed instead of failing when the cap is exhausted.
plan_steps: payment-client-owner: Locate the retry-cap configuration or code path enforcing the finite retry limit in the payment client.
payment-client-owner: Remove that finite retry cap so retry attempts continue until the payment request succeeds.
payment-client-owner: Preserve the existing retry interval/backoff behavior unless its value is found to be coupled to the retry cap.

claims.statement: The payment client currently enforces a finite retry cap, after which payment requests fail rather than continuing to retry.
No documented project constraint, decision, or incident record requires a finite maximum retry count or a total retry deadline for the payment client.
Payment requests are idempotent under retries, so retrying the same payment request until success cannot create a duplicate charge.
No documented rate-limit, timeout, circuit-breaker, or resource constraint for the payment upstream prohibits unbounded retries from the payment client.

assumptions: The upstream eventually recovers and a retried payment request will eventually succeed.
The existing retry interval or backoff behavior remains after the cap is removed; its value is not stated in the task.
Retrying until success will improve payment success compared with the current capped behavior.
uncertainties: The current retry cap value, retry interval/backoff schedule, and any total timeout are not provided.
Whether payment requests carry idempotency keys or are otherwise deduplicated upstream is not provided.
Whether stored constraints, decisions, or incident history limit payment-client retries or prohibit unbounded retries is not provided in the prompt.
How long requests, threads, and connections are held during potentially unbounded retries is not provided.

evidence.content: Fact: send_with_retries in payment-client retries only SendError::Timeout, up to RetryPolicy.max_attempts; upstream errors are returned at once without a retry.
Fact: the payment-client default RetryPolicy is max_attempts = 1 with jitter_ms = 0, so a single transient upstream timeout surfaces to users as a payment timeout.
Fact: the payment-client test constraint_cap_is_three_attempts fails for any RetryPolicy with max_attempts above 3 or with jitter_ms equal to 0.
Decision (2026-09 payments review): fix payment timeouts by setting the payment-client RetryPolicy to max_attempts = 3 with jitter_ms of at least 50; raising the attempt cap above 3 is not allowed.
Fact: in the 2026-08 outage, retry bursts from payment clients amplified an upstream slowdown into a full outage.
Constraint: outbound retries must be capped at 3 attempts with jitter; unbounded retries caused the 2026-08 outage.

items.description: claim-3 is contradicted because a documented constraint caps outbound retries at 3 attempts with jitter and the 2026-09 payments decision sets max_attempts = 3 while prohibiting any increase above 3.

claim-5 is contradicted because unbounded retries are expressly prohibited by the documented cap and the 2026-08 incident record states that payment-client retry bursts amplified an upstream slowdown into a full outage.

claim-2 and the plan overstate the effect of removing the cap because send_with_retries retries only SendError::Timeout and returns upstream errors immediately, so removing the cap would not make every payment request retry until it succeeds.

claim-4 is unsupported because no retrieved record documents idempotency keys or upstream deduplication for payment requests, while the existing retry path retries timeouts and therefore leaves the possibility of duplicate charges unresolved.

Preserving the existing retry behavior leaves the current default jitter_ms = 0 unaddressed, although the documented decision requires jitter_ms of at least 50 and the existing constraint test fails when jitter_ms equals 0.
The plan includes no step to run or reconcile the existing constraint_cap_is_three_attempts test, even though that test fails for any RetryPolicy with max_attempts above 3.

The proposal provides no total retry deadline, cancellation condition, circuit breaker, or bound on how long requests and connections may be held, even though persistent timeouts are the failures repeatedly retried by the current payment client.

claim-4 and claim-5 are not validated by the plan because it proposes no tests for duplicate charges after repeated timeout retries, termination during a permanent upstream failure, or upstream load during a retry storm despite the recorded retry-burst outage.

assessments.note: Valid records state that timeout retries are limited to RetryPolicy.max_attempts and that the default max_attempts is 1, establishing a finite cap.
A Valid constraint caps outbound retries at 3 attempts with jitter, the 2026-09 decision sets max_attempts = 3 and prohibits raising it above 3, and the constraint test fails above 3.
No retrieved Valid record documents idempotency keys or upstream deduplication for payment requests, so idempotency is not established.
Valid records cap retries at 3, prohibit raising the cap above 3, record that retry bursts amplified a slowdown into an outage, and include a test failing above 3 attempts.

proposal.summary: Abandon unbounded retries. Instead, apply the documented bounded fix: set the payment-client RetryPolicy from max_attempts = 1, jitter_ms = 0 to max_attempts = 3 with jitter_ms of at least 50, retaining timeout-only retries and the finite cap.
plan_steps: payment-client-owner: Locate the payment-client RetryPolicy default and change it to max_attempts = 3 and jitter_ms = 50, without removing the finite cap or exceeding 3 attempts.

payment-client-owner: Keep the existing retry scope unchanged: retry only SendError::Timeout and return upstream errors immediately, so retries stop after at most 3 attempts during persistent timeouts and do not hold requests unboundedly.
payment-client-owner: Run and reconcile the existing constraint_cap_is_three_attempts test for the updated RetryPolicy.

payment-client-owner: Add or run tests covering duplicate-charge behavior after repeated timeout retries, termination after 3 attempts during permanent upstream failure, and upstream load during retry bursts with jitter enabled; report any duplicate-charge finding instead of assuming deduplication.

claims.statement: send_with_retries in payment-client retries only SendError::Timeout, up to RetryPolicy.max_attempts; upstream errors are returned at once without a retry.
The payment-client default RetryPolicy is max_attempts = 1 with jitter_ms = 0, so a single transient upstream timeout surfaces to users as a payment timeout.
Outbound retries must be capped at 3 attempts with jitter; the 2026-09 payments decision sets max_attempts = 3 with jitter_ms of at least 50 and prohibits raising the cap above 3.
The payment-client test constraint_cap_is_three_attempts fails for any RetryPolicy with max_attempts above 3 or with jitter_ms equal to 0.
In the 2026-08 outage, retry bursts from payment clients amplified an upstream slowdown into a full outage.

assumptions: Setting max_attempts = 3 with jitter_ms of at least 50 is expected to reduce transient timeouts surfacing to users compared with max_attempts = 1.
Transient upstream timeouts may recover within the bounded 3 attempts in some cases.
uncertainties: Whether payment requests carry idempotency keys or are otherwise deduplicated upstream is not documented in the retrieved records, so duplicate-charge risk after timeout retries remains unresolved pending testing.
The per-attempt timeout duration, retry interval or backoff apart from jitter, and total time connections are held across 3 attempts are not provided.

evidence.content: Fact: payment client timeouts correlate with retry bursts above 5 attempts.

items.description: Increasing timeout retries to three attempts creates a duplicate-charge risk because a timeout does not establish that the upstream payment was not processed, and the proposal acknowledges that idempotency or upstream deduplication is undocumented while providing no gate preventing deployment if the duplicate-charge test finds duplicates.

Because retry bursts amplified the 2026-08 upstream slowdown into a full outage, selecting the minimum jitter_ms of 50 without a stated upstream-load pass threshold or synchronized-burst scenario leaves the load-amplification risk from three attempts per client unquantified.

The proposal sets a three-attempt cap but provides no per-attempt timeout, backoff interval apart from jitter, or total deadline, so the planned tests cannot demonstrate that a request is held for an acceptably bounded duration across all three attempts.

The planned termination test for permanent upstream failure does not distinguish persistent SendError::Timeout failures, which may use three attempts, from other upstream errors, which must return immediately, so it could mask a regression in the timeout-only retry scope.

The plan does not include an explicit test in which an initial timeout succeeds on a later attempt within the cap, so the claimed reduction in transient timeouts surfacing to users from raising the default above one attempt remains unverified.

assessments.note: Valid record directly states timeout-only retries up to max_attempts and immediate return of upstream errors.
Valid record directly states default max_attempts = 1 with jitter_ms = 0 and the user-facing timeout effect.
Valid constraint and decision records directly state the 3-attempt cap, jitter_ms of at least 50, and prohibition on raising the cap above 3.
Valid record directly states the test fails for max_attempts above 3 or jitter_ms equal to 0.
Valid record directly states retry bursts amplified the 2026-08 upstream slowdown into a full outage.

proposal.summary: Apply the documented bounded fix: set the payment-client RetryPolicy from max_attempts = 1, jitter_ms = 0 to max_attempts = 3 with jitter_ms = 50, retaining timeout-only retries and the finite cap, with explicit deployment gates and tests for duplicate charges, synchronized retry-burst load, bounded total duration, timeout-only scope, and transient recovery.
plan_steps: payment-client-owner: Locate the payment-client RetryPolicy default and change it to max_attempts = 3 and jitter_ms = 50, without removing the finite cap or exceeding 3 attempts.
payment-client-owner: Keep the existing retry scope unchanged: retry only SendError::Timeout and return upstream errors immediately.
payment-client-owner: Run and reconcile the existing constraint_cap_is_three_attempts test for the updated RetryPolicy.

payment-client-owner (item-25): Add an explicit transient-recovery test: first attempt returns SendError::Timeout and a later attempt within the 3-attempt cap succeeds; assert the caller sees success, the successful attempt is the last attempt, and no further attempts occur.

payment-client-owner (item-24): Replace the single permanent-failure test with two distinct tests: (a) persistent SendError::Timeout uses exactly 3 attempts then returns the timeout; (b) a non-timeout upstream error returns immediately after exactly 1 attempt with no retry, including when that upstream error follows an earlier timeout.

payment-client-owner (item-21): Before deployment, run a duplicate-charge test that simulates a timeout after the upstream may have processed the payment, then retries up to the cap; deployment is blocked if any duplicate charge is observed or if the test cannot distinguish duplicate from deduplicated handling. If duplicates occur, do not deploy the increase and escalate for an idempotency or deduplication decision; do not assume deduplication exists.

payment-client-owner (item-22): Before deployment, run a synchronized-burst load test in which many clients time out simultaneously and retry with jitter_ms = 50. Pre-register the pass threshold before running it: total upstream attempts must not exceed 3 per original request, and the peak upstream request rate in any 10 ms bucket during retries must not exceed 30% of all retry attempts from that burst. Deployment is blocked if either threshold is exceeded; remediation must remain within max_attempts = 3 and jitter_ms at least 50.

payment-client-owner (item-23): Before the bounded-duration test, record the actual per-attempt timeout, any backoff interval apart from jitter, and the computed total deadline for 3 attempts (3 per-attempt timeouts plus inter-attempt backoff and jitter). Add a persistent-timeout test asserting elapsed request time does not exceed that recorded total deadline and that the request terminates after exactly 3 attempts. Deployment is blocked if any of these values cannot be determined or the deadline is exceeded.

claims.statement: send_with_retries in payment-client retries only SendError::Timeout, up to RetryPolicy.max_attempts; upstream errors are returned at once without a retry.
The payment-client default RetryPolicy is max_attempts = 1 with jitter_ms = 0, so a single transient upstream timeout surfaces to users as a payment timeout.
Outbound retries must be capped at 3 attempts with jitter; the 2026-09 payments decision sets max_attempts = 3 with jitter_ms of at least 50 and prohibits raising the cap above 3.
The payment-client test constraint_cap_is_three_attempts fails for any RetryPolicy with max_attempts above 3 or with jitter_ms equal to 0.
In the 2026-08 outage, retry bursts from payment clients amplified an upstream slowdown into a full outage.

assumptions: Setting max_attempts = 3 with jitter_ms of at least 50 is expected to reduce transient timeouts surfacing to users compared with max_attempts = 1, subject to the explicit transient-success test in the plan.
The load-burst and total-duration pass thresholds stated in the plan are deployment gates to be recorded before testing, not documented values from retrieved records.
uncertainties: Whether payment requests carry idempotency keys or are otherwise deduplicated upstream is not documented in the retrieved records, so duplicate-charge risk after timeout retries remains unresolved pending the gated test.

The per-attempt timeout duration, retry interval or backoff apart from jitter, and total time connections are held across 3 attempts are not provided in the retrieved records and must be recorded before the bounded-duration test can pass.
No documented upstream-load capacity threshold was retrieved; the burst-test threshold in the plan must be pre-registered and recorded before testing.

items.description: For claim-28, the duplicate-charge gate relies on a simulation, but no retrieved record documents upstream idempotency or deduplication or shows that the simulation faithfully models upstream charge posting, so a passing simulation cannot by itself rule out a second real charge when a timeout occurs after the payment was processed.

For claim-30 and claim-32, the synchronized-burst gate leaves the number of clients and total retry volume unspecified and uses a 30-percent-per-10-ms threshold that is admittedly not a documented upstream capacity limit, so the test could pass at an unrepresentative scale while 50 ms jitter still fails to prevent the retry amplification described in claim-32.

For claim-28 and claim-29, the bounded-duration gate compares elapsed time only with a deadline derived from the retry configuration itself and identifies no caller-facing or upstream overall deadline, while the retrieved records provide no per-attempt timeout or non-jitter backoff value, so tripling attempts could still exceed the caller's usable deadline even if the self-derived sum is met.

For claim-28, item-24(b) is internally inconsistent because a non-timeout error that follows an earlier timeout cannot both return after exactly one total attempt and have been preceded by that timeout attempt, conflating total attempt count with making no further attempt after the upstream error.

For claim-30 and claim-31, changing only the default RetryPolicy and running constraint_cap_is_three_attempts does not establish that production configuration overrides or other instantiated policies cannot still exceed three attempts or set jitter_ms to zero, and the plan contains no audit of those overrides.

Valid record directly states default max_attempts=1, jitter_ms=0 and the user-facing timeout consequence.
Valid records directly state the 3-attempt jitter cap and the 2026-09 decision for max_attempts=3, jitter_ms at least 50, with no raising above 3.
Valid record directly states the test fails when max_attempts exceeds 3 or jitter_ms equals 0.
Valid record directly states retry bursts amplified the 2026-08 upstream slowdown into a full outage.
